answer: Unique history checkpointing makes every agent identity submit a short code summarizing its interaction history, and that code must differ from every other active identity's code. Because exact clones cannot diverge, any hollow duplicate code is rejected and the copies are paused until one proves a separate path. To pass, an attacker must pay a distinct river of transaction fees and wait through a cold tundra period for each clone, so every extra identity carries its own real interaction cost.
